data.title: AU$34.11 - That's What Analysts Think Technology One Limited (ASX:TNE) Is Worth After These Results
data.description:
The annual results for Technology One Limited (ASX:TNE) were released last week, making it a good time to revisit its performance. Technology One reported in line with analyst predictions, delivering revenues of AU$670m and statutory earnings per share of AU$0.50, suggesting the business is executing well and in line with its plan. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

After the latest results, the 16 analysts covering Technology One are now predicting revenues of AU$780.2m in 2027. If met, this would reflect a meaningful 16% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to ascend 20% to AU$0.60. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of AU$784.7m and earnings per share (EPS) of AU$0.60 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

Check out our latest analysis for Technology One

With the analysts reconfirming their revenue and earnings forecasts, it's surprising to see that the price target rose 9.5% to AU$34.11. It looks as though they previously had some doubts over whether the business would live up to their expectations. The consensus price target is just an average of individual analyst targets, so - it could be handy to see how wide the range of underlying estimates is. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Technology One at AU$40.00 per share, while the most bearish prices it at AU$22.50. There are definitely some different views on the stock, but the range of estimates is not wide enough as to imply that the situation is unforecastable, in our view.

Taking a look at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can understand these forecasts is to see how they compare to both past performance and industry growth estimates. The period to the end of 2027 brings more of the same, according to the analysts, with revenue forecast to display 16% growth on an annualised basis. That is in line with its 15% annual growth over the past five years. Compare this with the broader industry, which analyst estimates (in aggregate) suggest will see revenues grow 13% annually. It's clear that while Technology One's revenue growth is expected to continue on its current trajectory, it's only expected to grow in line with the industry itself.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. Happily, there were no real changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow in line with the overall industry. There was also a nice increase in the price target, with the analysts clearly feeling that the intrinsic value of the business is improving.

With that in mind, we wouldn't be too quick to come to a conclusion on Technology One. Long-term earnings power is much more important than next year's profits. That lack of consensus underlines how much of the valuation work still comes back to an investor’s own conviction on long term crypto adoption and how Coinbase Global monetises that through trading, custody, and subscription lines.

data.title: What BlackRock Stock's Private Markets Fund Filing Means For Shareholders
data.description:
• BlackRock has applied for regulatory approval of an exchange traded interval fund structure that blends ETF style intraday trading with periodic share repurchases and exposure to private market assets, aiming to give a wider range of investors access to holdings that are usually harder to reach.
  • The move leans on BlackRock’s scale in ETFs and its growing private markets platform, signaling a push to turn illiquid, higher fee alternative assets into a more systematized product line that can sit alongside its core index and technology businesses.
  • This article will examine how BlackRock’s development of an ETF interval fund for private assets could influence its broader investment narrative.

See how BlackRock’s interval fund push compares with other asset managers experimenting at the edge of public and private markets by reviewing the hand picked 19 high quality undiscovered gems now shaping this trend.

BlackRock Investment Narrative Recap

According to LunaRodas, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the AI infrastructure financing theme has become the main growth story, while other programs have slipped into the background.

The short term catalyst is execution on that AI and private markets push without letting margins slip from the recent 47.8% level. The largest current risk is concentration of the narrative around one growth engine combined with significant insider selling in recent months, which can amplify any wobble in flows or fee pressure.

Among the recent disclosures, BlackRock’s move to seek SEC approval for exchange traded interval funds that mix intraday trading with private assets is closest to the private markets thread LunaRodas highlights. It ties directly into management’s 2030 plan, which leans heavily on higher fee alternative strategies layered on top of the ETF franchise.

If interval funds are approved and rolled out effectively, they could reinforce the existing AI infrastructure and private markets story by giving BlackRock one more wrapper to distribute those assets. If regulators move slowly or investor demand for these hybrids is tepid, the near term impact on catalysts is likely limited and the AI financing pipeline remains the clearer operational swing factor.

data.description:

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Vulcan Steel

Notably, that recent sale by Non-Executive Chairman Rhys Jones was not the only time they sold Vulcan Steel shares this year. They previously made an even bigger sale of -AU$804k worth of shares at a price of AU$6.19 per share. While we don't usually like to see insider selling, it's more concerning if the sales take place at a lower price. It's of some comfort that this sale was conducted at a price well above the current share price, which is AU$5.47. So it is hard to draw any strong conclusion from it.

Over the last year, we can see that insiders have bought 43.04k shares worth AU$230k. But insiders sold 350.00k shares worth AU$2.0m. data.title: Can Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) Justify Its Valuation After Margin Gains And FireCuda Forge?
data.description:

Recent trading has been choppy for Seagate Technology Holdings, with the share price falling about 21% over the past month and 39% over 90 days, even after fresh product news and record margin commentary helped the stock post a 1-day share price return of 1.08% and lift the latest share price to US$504.40. Against that pullback, momentum over longer horizons remains strong, with a year to date share price return of 75.42% and a 1-year total shareholder return of 99.86%. Seagate is the storage-capacity position in a portfolio built on physical scarcity, and it is the one I would defend furthest into a downturn.
